chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Udays, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when the shadow of the wall was one cubit, would perform the zuhr prayer, and when it was two cubits, he would perform the 'asr prayer.
I said: The walls differ; some of them are short and some of them are tall.

He said: The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم at that time was a qamah in height, and the one cubit and two cubits were only set so that there would not be a supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الْجِدَارِ: the wall whose shadow was used as a measure
key_terms.ذِرَاعًا: one cubit, a unit for determining the prayer time
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْنِ: two cubits, a unit for determining the prayer time of 'asr
key_terms.فَيْءُ: the returning shadow used to mark prayer time

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم determine the time of zuhr and 'asr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the timing of zuhr and 'asr prayer by referring to the shadow length of the wall of the Prophet’s mosque. It clarifies that these measurements were used as practical markers to distinguish the time of obligatory prayers and prevent voluntary prayer from encroaching upon them.
